frameworks.name: 20-Hour Competence
frameworks.definition: Most people can achieve functional competence in any skill, including money-making skills, within 20 hours of deliberate practice, provided they delay initial quitting and extend the threshold before declaring something hard.

frameworks.name: Infinite vs Finite Game Frame
frameworks.definition: Entrepreneurship is fundamentally an infinite game where persistence and not quitting are the winning conditions, not being the best at any single moment.

frameworks.name: Work Ethic as Currency
frameworks.definition: Work ethic is the primary currency of respect across all human societies; respect is earned exclusively through demonstrated action and contribution, not desire, intention, or effort level.

claims.text: Most people can learn any skill in 20 hours, but the real constraint is that they delay the first 20 hours by years, not that the learning itself is hard.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Delaying action for years compounds into perceived impossibility; the skill is learnable, the barrier is initiating practice.
bounded_by: Does not apply to skills with prerequisite foundations (e.g., advanced mathematics assumes basic arithmetic)
Does not account for variance in individual prior knowledge or learning disability

claims.text: Reality is measured only by action taken, not by desire, deservingness, or effort level. A person genuinely motivated must measure themselves against input (the actions they control) rather than outcomes or intentions.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: when self-assessing genuine motivation or capability
claims.mechanism: Outcomes and effort are influenced by external factors; input (daily actions) is the only variable an individual controls entirely, making it the true measure of commitment.
bounded_by: Does not absolve responsibility for environmental or systemic constraints
Does not imply outcomes are irrelevant, only that self-judgment should anchor to controllables

claims.text: Shortening the time between deciding to learn something and beginning practice, while extending the threshold before declaring difficulty or quitting, enables accomplishment of significantly more than most people attempt.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Reduced delay to action lowers sunk-cost inertia; extended difficulty threshold prevents premature quitting during the initial learning curve's 'despair' phase.
bounded_by: Does not apply if the underlying task is genuinely impossible or mismatch to individual capability ceiling

claims.text: Across all timeframes in history, all countries, all cultures, all age groups, and all genders, people universally respect those who work and contribute visibly through effort.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Work and visible contribution signal utility and reliability; respect is conferred on those who demonstrate capacity to do, not on those who articulate intention.
bounded_by: Overstatement: 'universally' is a strong claim lacking empirical citation; more accurately phrased as 'widely across observed cultures'
Does not account for contexts where systemic barriers prevent work visibility (prison, disability, discrimination)

claims.text: Entrepreneurs who reframe their situation as an infinite game (where not quitting is the only winning condition) rather than a finite game (best performer wins at a defined endpoint) develop superior persistence.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: for business owners operating without external milestones or defined market endpoints
claims.mechanism: Finite game frame incentivizes optimization for a single metric at a single point; infinite game frame removes the exit option, making persistence and endurance the sole viable strategy.
bounded_by: Does not apply to races with hard deadlines (product launches, regulatory filing dates, competitor disruption windows)
The claim is reframed from Hormozi's observation; original lacks rigorous comparison data

claims.text: For founders facing hardship, reframing the cost of failure (returning as a failure to one's origin) as worse than any obstacle encountered transforms quitting from an option into a non-option, enabling pure persistence.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: for founders with a defined failure state they find unacceptable (e.g., 'returning home a failure')
where reputational/identity cost exceeds other costs
claims.mechanism: Eliminating quitting from the choice set removes the decision-making burden; remaining option forces pure endurance and strategy iteration.
bounded_by: Does not apply to contexts where failure is survivable and acceptable
Psychological cost of this frame (shame, sunk-cost fallacy) is not addressed

claims.text: Work ethic is the primary currency through which respect is earned, whether that work is on oneself, on a skill, on a product, or on a business.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: universally across gender, culture, and context
claims.mechanism: Work and contribution are observable signals of reliability and capability; respect follows from demonstrated utility.
bounded_by: Does not account for contexts where work is invisible or systemically undervalued
Does not address scenarios where respect is granted based on inheritance, position, or identity alone

claims.text: When a founder removes quitting from their available options and frames the situation as an infinite game with one rule (persist), they develop absolute commitment that transcends situational difficulty.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: for founders making an irrevocable commitment to a business
where the cost of failure is psychologically unacceptable
claims.mechanism: Psychological constraint removal (eliminating the 'quit' option) creates a state of forced persistence that prevents vacillation and decision-making paralysis.
bounded_by: Does not account for cases where persistence is irrational or the business model is fundamentally broken
Does not address burnout, mental health, or secondary consequences of forced persistence

claims.text: When you measure yourself against observable action input rather than outcomes, intentions, or self-reported effort, you will often be embarrassed by the reality of what you are actually doing versus what you believe you are doing.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Outcomes and effort are partially outside personal control; actions are fully controllable; reality reveals the gap between perceived and actual action.
bounded_by: Does not apply to external circumstances that constrain observable action
Does not account for selection bias in which actions become visible

examples.text: Alex Hormozi's personal experience: as a founder facing severe hardship, his frame was that returning to Baltimore as a failure was psychologically worse than any obstacle he could encounter. This made quitting not a real option on his decision table, forcing persistence and strategic iteration rather than vacillation.

When a founder is asked in Q&As 'what kept you going when things were tough?', many construct compelling narratives about motivation or vision. Hormozi's honest answer was simpler: he never considered quitting, because the alternative (failure/returning home) was worse than any situation he actually faced.

practices.text: When you claim you cannot learn something, set a 20-hour timer and commit to deliberate practice for the full duration before reassessing. Most perceived learning impossibilities resolve into mere lack of attempted hours.

Measure yourself only by the amount of action you take (input), not by how much you want the outcome, how deserving you think you are, or how hard you believe you are trying. Reality is indifferent to anything but what you do.

If you find yourself claiming the 'demon card' of having been through hard times, prove it by being hard now in your current situation. Use the frame that others have endured worse, therefore you can endure your current challenge.
Reframe entrepreneurship explicitly as an infinite game where not quitting is the only winning condition, not as a finite game where you are trying to outperform competitors at a defined moment.
Eliminate quitting from your choice set: ask yourself what the cost of returning to your starting point (failure) would be, and use that reframing to make persistence your only natural option.
